license_note: Supplier-catalogue reality plus paraphrased standards tables, not a standard. Nobody owns the fact that 1 in 6061 bar exists; size availability is recall of McMaster-Carr, Online Metals, Metal Supermarkets (NA) and generic EU/UK stockists. Tolerance numbers are paraphrased from recall of ASTM B211 (cold-finished bar), ASTM B221 (extruded rod and tube), ASTM B209 (sheet/plate), ASTM B210 (drawn seamless tube), ASTM B241 (pipe), EN 754-2 / EN 755-2 (metric drawn / extruded bar), EN 485-3 / EN 485-4 (hot-rolled plate / cold-rolled sheet), EN 755-7 / 754-7 (metric tube, proxy only), with pipe dimensions from ASME B36.10M; minimum properties from recall of the same ASTM/EN specs. Standards tables are facts and are cited as such; the standards' text is copyrighted by ASTM / CEN and is not reproduced. Every number is labelled 'likely' or 'recall'; none is 'certain'; editions are unverified.

columns.key: unique id; original compiled keys are retained, '_ext' / '_drawn' suffixes are the split-form twins
columns.material: single alloy+temper the row's tolerance and minimum properties apply to (no packed alternatives)
columns.eu_equivalent: what an EU/UK stockist will actually quote for this size; null if same as material
columns.form: enum, ONE production route per row: cold_finished | extruded | rolled_sheet | rolled_plate | drawn_seamless | extruded_tube | pipe_extruded | metric_tube_6082
columns.dim_in: inch: bar diameter / plate thickness / tube or pipe OD, exactly as the standard or catalogue states it; null for metric rows
columns.dim_in_label: fractional or NPS label as printed in catalogues; null for metric rows
columns.dim_mm: mm: same dimension; inch rows are dim_in x 25.4 rounded HALF-UP to 3 decimals on the decimal value (0.1875 in -> 4.7625 -> 4.763); metric rows nominal
columns.wall_in: tube/pipe only: physical nominal wall in inches (3/16 wall is stored as 0.1875, not the catalogue label 0.188); null otherwise
columns.wall_in_label: tube/pipe only: wall as the catalogue prints it (e.g. '0.188', 'sch 40'); null otherwise
columns.wall_mm: tube/pipe only: wall_in x 25.4 half-up to 3 decimals, or metric nominal; null otherwise
columns.wall_tol_mm: tube/pipe only: worst-case wall deviation in mm (10 % of wall for B210/B221 drawn/extruded tube, 12.5 % for B241 pipe, max(10 %, 0.3 mm) for the metric proxy); null otherwise
columns.id_nominal_in: tube/pipe only: OD - 2 x wall_in (derived, NOT a controlled dimension); null otherwise
columns.id_nominal_mm: tube/pipe only: derived nominal ID in mm (half-up, 3 decimals); null otherwise
columns.id_min_mm: tube/pipe only: (dim_mm - tol_minus_mm) - 2 x (wall_mm + wall_tol_mm); the smallest bore you can get on mean diameter; ovality can make an individual diameter smaller still (see ovality_individual_dia_tol_mm)
columns.ovality_individual_dia_tol_mm: tube/pipe only: allowed deviation of ANY individual diameter from nominal (mm). = tol_plus_mm on mean-diameter rows; = 2 x tol_plus_mm where wall < 2.5 % of OD (B210/B221 thin-wall rule, recall). null otherwise
columns.tol_plus_mm: worst-case plus deviation of dim_mm allowed by tolerance_basis (mm, number)
columns.tol_minus_mm: worst-case minus deviation of dim_mm (mm, number); already includes any all-minus supplier quote the compiled table carried
columns.tol_plus_in: inch rows: tol_plus_mm expressed in the standard's inch value; null for metric rows
columns.tol_minus_in: inch rows: tol_minus_mm in inches; null for metric rows
columns.tolerance_basis: enum: astm_b211 | astm_b221_rod | astm_b221_tube | astm_b209 | astm_b210 | astm_b241 | en_754_2 | en_755_2 | en_485_3 | en_485_4 | en_755_7_proxy
columns.tolerance_confidence: likely | recall for the tol_* numbers specifically (row 'confidence' is the minimum over all load-bearing fields)
columns.tolerance_note: free-text provenance for the tolerance (band, boundary handling, supplier practice); never parse this, use tol_* numbers
columns.dim_min_mm: dim_mm - tol_minus_mm: the smallest bar diameter / plate thickness / tube OD you may receive
columns.cleanup_per_side_mm: recommended minimum machining allowance per side for this form (mm); designer may increase, should not decrease
columns.max_finish_mm: dim_min_mm - 2 x cleanup_per_side_mm: largest finished diameter (bar), thickness (plate) or OD (tube/pipe) that fully cleans up from this stock
columns.min_finish_id_mm: tube/pipe only: id_max_mm + 2 x cleanup_per_side_mm: smallest bore that fully cleans up the as-drawn ID; null otherwise
columns.clears_casing_mm: tube/pipe only: largest nominal motor casing OD in [29, 38, 54, 75, 98] mm such that casing + 0.5 mm <= id_min_mm (as-received bore, mean diameter); null = clears none, or not a tube
columns.spec_min_uts_mpa: specification minimum ultimate tensile strength (MPa) for THIS form and alloy/temper, from recall of the ASTM/EN spec named in props_basis
columns.spec_min_yield_mpa: specification minimum 0.2 % yield (MPa) for this form; recall
columns.props_basis: which spec/table the minimum properties come from; edition unverified
columns.mass_per_m_g: bar/tube/pipe: grams per metre at 2.70 g/cm3 nominal density, from nominal dims; null for plate
columns.mass_per_m2_g: plate: grams per square metre at 2.70 g/cm3 from nominal thickness; null otherwise
columns.availability_na: common | limited | special order - North America (McMaster-Carr, Online Metals, Metal Supermarkets, local shops). 'limited' = one online supplier only (typically McMaster)
columns.availability_eu: common | limited | special order - EU/UK stockists. 'limited' = UK imperial-size stockists only, or larger stockists only
columns.availability_note: regional/supplier caveats and named substitutes (every named substitute is a row in this table); null if none
columns.alt_material_note: availability-only remarks on 7075 and 304 for this size; carries NO tolerance values (see notes 10)
columns.disputed: null, or a list of {field, compiled, alternative, alt_source, resolution} where a skeptic's recall differed from the compiler's and neither has a stronger source
columns.confidence: likely | recall (never 'certain' in this table): the weakest load-bearing field in the row
columns.source: standard(s) or catalogue(s) the row leans on; editions unverified (notes 15)

notes: READ BEFORE USING. (1) Nothing in this table is a finished dimension: every diameter, face and bore that matters gets machined. The design question is 'does the stock contain the part with cleanup': use max_finish_mm (bar/plate/tube OD) and min_finish_id_mm (tube bore), which are computed from the MINIMUM stock (dim_min_mm) and the recommended cleanup_per_side_mm (0.5 mm cold-finished bar / drawn tube / sheet / plate <= 1/2 in; 1.0 mm extruded bar or tube <= 4 in and plate > 1/2 in; 1.5 mm larger extrusions and pipe). (2) Tolerances: tol_plus_mm / tol_minus_mm are worst-case NUMBERS derived from recall of ASTM B211 / B221 / B209 / B210 / B241 and EN 754-2 / 755-2 / 485-3 / 485-4 (editions unverified, see 15). Where a supplier all-minus quote was known it is folded into tol_minus_mm. Where two recollections differed the WIDER band was stored and the alternative is in 'disputed' (this affects every ASTM B221 extruded rod row, every EN 754-2 / 755-2 metric bar row, the pipe OD rows). Wider is conservative for a stock-contains-part check; it is NOT the standard's quoted value. At an exact band boundary (2, 4, 6, 8 in extruded rod; 3, 4, 5, 6 in drawn tube; 0.625 in plate) the wider band was taken. Get the mill cert or measure the delivered stock before cutting a pressure part. (3) Form is ONE production route per row. Where a size is sold both ways the row is split: the original key keeps the form the compiled table listed first and the '_ext' / '_drawn' twin carries the other. 2-1/2 and 3 in bar differ by 5x in diameter tolerance between the two forms; ask the supplier which you are getting. ASTM B221 has separate tolerance tables for extruded ROD (tolerance_basis astm_b221_rod) and extruded TUBE (astm_b221_tube): a 4 in rod and a 4 in tube from the same standard legitimately carry different figures. (4) Tube ID is DERIVED (OD - 2 x wall), not controlled. id_min_mm / id_max_mm bracket it on MEAN diameter with wall at +/-10 %; ovality_individual_dia_tol_mm is the extra you must allow on ANY single diameter where wall < 2.5 % of OD (B210/B221 thin-wall rule, recall: 2 x the mean-diameter tolerance). clears_casing_mm uses id_min_mm and a 0.5 mm radial clearance over the nominal casing (29/38/54/75/98 mm); it does not account for ovality, so a thin-wall tube that 'clears' on paper may still bind on a casing: bore it or measure. Examples: 2.250x0.065 and 2.250x0.049 do NOT clear a 54 mm casing; 3.000x0.065 does not clear 75; 4.000x0.083 does not clear 98. (5) Pressure vessels (tank end caps, couplers under pressure): design on wall_mm - wall_tol_mm (or measured), not nominal; use drawn seamless (ASTM B210) not extruded, porthole or welded tube; use the spec_min_* values for the FORM you actually bought: extruded 6061-T6/T6511 (B221) and pipe (B241) are 262 MPa UTS, not the 290 MPa of cold-finished bar, drawn tube and T651 plate. All property minima are recall. (6) Inch and metric are not interchangeable: 12 mm is not 1/2 in, 25 mm is not 1 in, 50 mm is not 2 in. Every metric row's availability_note names the NA inch substitute and says whether it is LARGER (contains the part) or SMALLER (does not). The 'material' field carries one alloy; 'eu_equivalent' says what an EU/UK stockist will actually quote (6082-T6 for bar/tube/sheet; 6082-T651 OR 5083-H111 for plate). EU substitute 6082-T6: Rm >= ~290-310 MPa, Rp0.2 >= ~250-260 MPa by size band (EN 754-2/755-2/485-2, recall). 5083-H111 plate: Rm >= ~275 MPa but Rp0.2 >= ~125 MPa (recall) - never use 6061 allowables for 5083. (7) Sheet vs plate: the inch boundary is 0.250 in (below: 6061-T6 sheet, can bow; 0.250 in and up: T651 plate, stretch stress-relieved). The metric (EN 485) boundary is 6 mm, so 6 mm IS plate/T651 even though 6 mm < 0.250 in. Cast tooling plate (MIC-6: proprietary Al-Zn-Mg-type casting, UTS about 165 MPa, yield about 105 MPa; ATP-5 / K100-S: 5083-type castings, UTS about 275-285 MPa but yield about 125 MPa; all recall) is +/-0.005 in thick and flat but must NOT be designed with 6061-T651 allowables (290 / 241 MPa); it is fine for non-load-bearing bulkheads and sleds, not for tank ends. (8) Cold-finished bar (B211) has better roundness and tighter diameter than extruded T6511 (B221); extruded bar has residual stress and can move when a lot of material is removed asymmetrically. Straightness (recall, order of magnitude only): cold-finished rod about 0.01 in per ft, extruded rod about 0.0125 in per ft, drawn tube about 0.01 in per ft; plate flatness per B209 is thickness- and width-dependent (thin plate can be 0.1-0.25 in out over 36 in). Long av-bay sleds and long couplers: face and bore in one setup, do not trust the stock. (9) Large discs (bulkheads, centering rings over about 4 in / 100 mm) are cut from plate, not big bar. Tube (e.g. 6 x 0.250) is a sensible blank for thin large rings if the radial width fits inside the wall with cleanup. (10) alt_material_note is availability prose only. All ASTM A484 (304 bar) and A480 (304 plate) tolerance values were REMOVED because two recollections of the A484 bands disagreed (compiler: +0/-0.002 to 1.5 in, -0.003 to 2.5, -0.005 to 4, -0.006 to 6; skeptic: -0.002 <= 1/2, -0.003 to 1, -0.004 to 1.5, -0.005 to 4, -0.006 to 6). Only the sign is agreed: A484 cold-finished rounds are ALL-MINUS. 304 gets its own table if the club needs it. 7075-T651 bar and plate come in the same inch sizes as 6061 up to about 4 in bar / 2 in plate; 7075 drawn tube is rare (2024-T3 is the usual high-strength drawn tube); 7075 is not weldable and is notch-sensitive. (11) Wall 0.188 in is the catalogue label for 3/16 = 0.1875 in: wall_in stores 0.1875 and wall_in_label '0.188', so ID = OD - 0.375 (the compiled table used 0.376). Rounding: all inch->mm values are the decimal product rounded HALF-UP to 3 decimals (0.1875 x 25.4 = 4.7625 -> 4.763); IEEE round-half-even would give 4.762. (12) Availability is split by region: availability_na (McMaster-Carr / Online Metals / Metal Supermarkets / local shops) and availability_eu (EU/UK stockists). 'limited' means one online supplier (metric 6061 in NA is McMaster only) or UK-imperial-only. Stock lengths: NA bar/tube 12 ft (3658 mm) mill lengths sold cut to 1 / 2 / 3 / 6 ft (305 / 610 / 914 / 1829 mm); metric 3 m and 6 m, cut 0.5 / 1 m; plate sold as 6x6, 12x12, 12x24 in and 100 / 200 / 300 mm squares. All availability is recall. (13) Pipe rows (ASTM B241 6061-T6, dims per ASME B36.10M) exist because a '3.5 / 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.5 in tube' request at a NA shop is usually filled with 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 NPS pipe (3.500 / 4.500 / 5.563 / 6.625 OD). Pipe wall tolerance is -12.5 %, not -10 %, and the surface is rougher. The 5.5 and 6.5 in OD tube rows were dropped in favour of the pipe rows. (14) Metric tube rows (tube_6082_m_*) carry PROXY tolerances (tolerance_basis en_755_7_proxy): deliberately wide recall values because the real EN 755-7 / 754-7 bands could not be verified. They exist so an EU user can pick a size; they are not the standard's numbers. Check the alloy on the quote: thin-wall metric tube is often 6060/6063-T6 (UTS about 215-245 MPa), not 6082. (15) Editions: none of the ASTM/EN tolerance or property numbers were checked against a current edition; they are recall of Aluminum Standards & Data-era tables (2010s) and EN 754/755/485 (2008-2016 editions). No row is 'certain'. (16) The size list is NOT exhaustive: intermediate bar sizes (5/16, 7/16, 7/8, 1-3/4, 2-1/4, 2-3/4 in), 5/16 and 1-1/4 in plate, 1-1/4 in OD tube and the thin-wall specials (3.5 / 4.5 / 5.0 x 0.049) were added; other combinations exist. A missing OD x wall means 'not in this table', not 'does not exist'. (17) Joining to the airframe/coupler table: a coupler blank is chosen so that tube dim_min_mm - 2 x cleanup (= max_finish_mm) >= airframe ID + your fit allowance, and a motor-mount sleeve so that id_min_mm >= casing OD + clearance (clears_casing_mm). Use dim_min_mm / id_min_mm / max_finish_mm / min_finish_id_mm as the join fields, never dim_mm or id_nominal_mm. (18) Dropped rows (do not design around them): bar_6061_m_180, bar_6061_m_200 (use plate), tube_6061_i_2.750x0.065 / x0.125 / x0.250 (thin catalogue row everywhere), tube_6061_i_5.500x0.125 / x0.250 and tube_6061_i_6.500x0.125 / x0.250 (you will be sold 5.563 / 6.625 OD pipe: see pipe rows). (19) Row 'confidence' is the weakest load-bearing field: 'likely' only where an independent second recall agreed with the tolerance band (B211 cold-finished <= 3.5 in, B209 plate, B210 drawn-tube mean OD) AND the size/availability was also 'likely'; everything extruded, metric, pipe or added is 'recall'.
